events.title: The Crusaders before Antioch
events.shortBlurb: Two years after Clermont, the host of the First Crusade crossed the Taurus and sat down before the walls of Antioch for its most terrible siege…
body: The armies that answered Urban II at Clermont fared better than the poor pilgrims who went before them. In June 1097 they took Nicaea; on the first of July they routed the Turks at Dorylaeum; then, through a burning summer, they crossed the length of Asia Minor.

On 20 October 1097 they came before Antioch, the ancient city of the disciples, girdled — the old account numbers them — by a wall with four hundred and fifty towers, and provisioned for a long defense by its governor Yaghi-Siyan. Too strong to storm and too large to surround, the city held the crusaders before it for more than seven months of hunger, desertion, and winter rain.

Antioch fell at last on the night of 2-3 June 1098, betrayed by the captain of a single tower; and within days the besiegers were themselves besieged by the relieving army of Kerbogha of Mosul, whom they defeated on 28 June. The way to Jerusalem lay open, though the host did not take it until the next year.
